thread:
maria: Quick sync — procurement at Kestrel APAC asked for a clear uptime + latency commitment and an example credit calc we can include in the renewal packet. Can we put together numbers and a short customer-facing blurb by EOD?
ajit: got it. do we have their committed monthly fee?
linh: procurement quoted $48k/mo during negotiation. they care about APAC region specifically.
evan: quick note — our region-specific p99 for embeddings last 7d: median ~270ms, spikes to ~380ms on warmup. uptime at 99.96% for the region over the quarter.
maria: perfect, thanks. procurement wants 2 things: (1) explicit SLO lines (uptime %, p99 latency target) and (2) sample credit calc so legal can see how exposure looks.
ajit: here's the standard formula we use, ok to share?
```
credit = monthly_committed_fee * breach_pct * severity_factor
# severity_factor defaults to 1 for availability, 0.5 for latency
```
linh: sharing that is fine; legal will polish wording. can we run scenarios for breach_pct = 0.1%, 0.5%, 1%?
evan: will run calc + pull exact uptime windows from metrics. question: do we propose p99 target of 350ms for APAC embeddings or stay conservative at 400ms?
maria: they'd prefer tighter SLAs but procurement is sensitive to big credit exposure. propose we offer: uptime 99.95% regional, p99 latency <= 350ms (on steady-state), plus appendix describing mitigations and warmup behavior.
ajit: running numbers with the $48k figure now. quick mental calc: 1% breach -> $480/mo (before severity). with severity_factor=0.5 for latency that'd be $240.
evan: confirmed. I'll attach a short ops note explaining fallback routes: auto-route to hosted tier in other region, canary fallback to smaller model variant, and prefix cache recommendations for onboarding traffic. include expected residual latencies for each fallback.
linh: I'll draft a one-paragraph procurement-friendly clause and paste it here for review.
maria: awesome — please include an example sentence like "Credits are calculated pro rata against the monthly committed fee and apply only to the impacted region and metric." keep it simple.
linh: drafting: "If Redwood fails to meet the regional uptime or latency commitment, Customer will be eligible for a credit calculated pro rata against the Customer's monthly committed fee for the impacted region. Credits apply only to the affected metric and are subject to the standard severity multipliers in the SLA schedule."
ajit: looks good. I'll also add the quick scenario table (numbers) and a note about excluded maintenance windows.
evan: I extracted metrics and will attach raw p99/time slices to the renewal packet. will also call out recent warmup spike on 2024-10-28 02:13 UTC and recommended mitigation (pre-warm cache).
maria: thanks everyone. final checklist: @evan metrics + mitigations, @ajit credit scenarios + exclusions, @linh procurement clause draft. reconvene 90m after EOD if anything outstanding. :thumbsup:
